subsection.title: Target User and Core Problem
subsection.description: - Start from one concrete hypothetical case: identify who, in what situation, is trying to do what, what problem they are assumed to face, and the present consequence. - Infer exactly one Primary Persona from that case. Do not require an actual or recent experience or ask the user to enumerate persona candidates. - Mention the current workaround or evidence only when it materially clarifies the problem. - Only if the user explicitly presents several candidate personas, ask them to anchor the case to exactly one. Do not silently select or combine the candidates.

subsection.title: Value and Core Hypothesis
subsection.description: - State the value the Primary Persona should gain and why that matters to the team or organization. - State the single most important belief this PoC should test. - Keep it concise. Do not require a metric, customer promise, hypothesis inventory, or FAQ unless the user already has one. - Do not invent business claims or measures the user did not provide or approve.
